question: A black hole as a river of space

scene.title: Why Light Can’t Escape a Black Hole
scene.subtitle: Picture space flowing into a black hole like a river toward a waterfall, faster closer in. Light swims through it at light speed, and at the black hole’s edge the flow is just as fast.
scene.takeaway: A black hole’s horizon is where space flows in at light speed. Inside it, even light swimming outward is carried in.

beats.title: A fish near a waterfall
beats.body: A river speeds up as it nears a waterfall. A fish swims upstream at a steady speed through the water: far from the edge, it outswims the slow current.

beats.title: The point of no return
beats.body: Closer in, the current matches the fish’s speed, and the fish holds still. Past that point the current is faster, and the fish is swept over the edge even as it keeps swimming.

beats.title: A river of space
beats.body: Space around a black hole can be pictured the same way: flowing inward, faster closer in. Light is the fish: it always moves at light speed through the space around it.

beats.title: The horizon
beats.body: The horizon is the point of no return: there, space flows in at light speed. Light sent outward escapes from outside it, stands still on it, and is carried in from inside it.

beats.title: No speed limit is broken
beats.body: Inside, space flows in faster than light, yet light still moves through it at exactly light speed. Space is not a fluid: the flow is an exact picture of how Einstein’s theory describes a black hole.

scene.why: It explains a black hole’s edge, the event horizon: the place past which nothing, not even light, can get back out.
scene.opening: Light always moves at light speed. So why can’t it escape from inside a black hole?

questions.q: Just outside the horizon, can light sent outward escape?
questions.a: Yes, slowly: space there flows in a little slower than light.

questions.q: What happens to light sent outward exactly at the horizon?
questions.a: It stands still: space flows in exactly at light speed.

questions.q: Does anything move through space faster than light inside the horizon?
questions.a: No: light still moves at light speed through the space around it; it is the space that flows in faster.
